INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEW — physical KNB1 inspector (scope A) + c0a7431 replay follow-through (scope B)
Reviewer: Claude Code, Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), fresh cold session, no subagents, 2026-10-19.
Frozen commit: 01bc49bd96c9995f7a4c439a8640293d90c63ee0 (branch feat/kan-v2-recovery-opening).
Explicit source repository: /Users/m/code/kan-tools/kan/.worktrees/kan-v2-recovery-opening
Export reviewed: <repo>/.local-state/reviews/recovery-opening (all commands ran here).

VERDICTS
  Scope A (physical read-only KNB1 inspector) ........ BLOCK
  Scope B (c0a7431 A-F1/A-F2/A-F3 follow-through) .... APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS
  Overall checkpoint (01bc49b) ........................ BLOCK
The BLOCK is a fail-closed correctness defect against an explicit opener requirement: the reader refuses
every bundle that retains an EMPTY original BLOB (A-F1). No incorrect hostile acceptance, no source-record
rewrite and no standalone escape was found in scope A. No parent recovery/frontend AC closes. No physical
writer, durability, job, RPC or frontend completion is claimed by this checkpoint, and none is credited here.

=====================================================================================================
0. INDEPENDENCE, RECORDING, IDENTITY
- I did not write any code under review. This is a cold session; no subagents; no fork.
- Git-first recording (day#168/kan#197): this REPORT.txt plus review-evidence/ is the record. I made no
  kan/day writes and no live-log reads. I do not claim current live-log access. The north star below
  comes only from the supplied frozen north-star.json.
- Identity BEFORE (logs/identity-before.txt) and AFTER (logs/91-identity-after.txt), using
  scripts/verify_identity.py: the export's 3,496 tracked files match the manifest SHA-256 exactly, AND
  every file's Git blob id equals `git ls-tree -r 01bc49b` in the explicit repo. Repo HEAD = 01bc49b.
  The only extra file is north-star.json (review-evidence/ is excluded as this review's own output).
  Result: IDENTITY OK both times.
- Environment: shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<kan-v2-library-resilience>/.local-state/target, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4,
  `cargo clean -p kan` first (logs/01-clean.txt: removed 939 files), one heavy job at a time. No own target,
  no installs, no .lake, no network, no live archives/keys/traffic, no parent edits, no Git writes, no
  stash operations (parent stash count read at end: 3, untouched), and no revert_v2.py.
- Observed concurrent activity in the PARENT worktree. It is NOT this reviewer's: the files are mode 0644
  (my umask gives 0600), they contain none of my mutation markers, and my drivers resolve every path to
  the export. At 10:03:12 an untracked .design/kan-v2-recovery-mutations.md appeared (a creator/restorer
  plan). From 10:19 to 10:26, uncommitted edits appeared to src/evidence_store/bundle.rs, tests/
  evidence_recovery_bundle.rs, .design/tools/recovery_bundle_files.py and ci.yml, plus untracked
  recovery_bundle_review_vectors.py and fixtures/recovery-bundle-review-v1.json
  (logs/90-parent-git-after.txt). The bundle.rs edit adds `(false, ValueRef::Null) if len == 0 => &[]`,
  which appears to address A-F1 below. This concurrent work is UNREVIEWED here and does not change the
  verdict on the frozen commit. Under ADR-52 it needs its own review round.
- Own housekeeping, disclosed: my first Python attempt (failed method, logs/06a) used /opt/homebrew
  python3.14, and importing .design/tools wrote 3 __pycache__ .pyc files into the export. I removed them
  (logs/50). I also killed only my own backgrounded schema-timing python process (pkill -f on my private
  /tmp/kanrev-vm path). No other process was touched.

1. NORTH STAR (from supplied frozen north-star.json only)
telos/raw-data-and-projections (Decision bafyreied3rklhs57...): "Raw attested data is retained in full and
never collapsed in the store. Every simplification ... is a determined projection computed on demand over
that raw data". It is in recorded tension with telos/performance-at-scale (InTensionWith, inbound and
outbound). The file reports excluded_by_trust=2 at top level. I cannot see those subjects and did not
reconstruct them. This work serves the telos as a read-only projection (Inspection/Replay) over retained
raw bundle bytes, which must never invent or drop retained evidence. Tension in play: acquisition budgets
and the non-streaming slice (performance/bounded memory) versus retaining every raw cell exactly. The
design keeps that tension explicit (no universal cap; streaming is the declared next step). A-F1 is the
place where it breaks: a legitimately retained raw state (an empty original) cannot be projected at all.

2. BASELINE (raw logs in logs/)
- v2-crypto: evidence_recovery_bundle 10/10, evidence_recovery_replay 10/10,
  evidence_recovery_replay_review_regressions 6/6, surface_conformance 19/19 (02-baseline-tests.txt).
- --lib evidence_store::bundle::snapshot_tests 2/2 (03).
- cargo clippy --features v2-crypto --all-targets -- -D warnings: exit 0 (04). cargo fmt --check: exit 0 (05).
- Python. FAILED METHOD (06a): under /opt/homebrew python3, the replay generators die with "No module
  named 'cryptography'". Rerun with KAN_CRYPTO_ORACLE_PYTHON (06b): recovery_bundle_schema.py 7/7 OK
  (it includes test_runtime_schema_matches_proposed_fixture); recovery_replay_vectors.py --check gives
  "45 independent state cases; 13 positive"; recovery_replay_review_vectors.py --check gives "23 design-
  derived review cases; conservative envelope bound 3816 bytes".
- Runtime SQL equals the previously proposed fixture. `cmp` reports them identical, and they are the same
  Git blob b714c19f at both 01bc49b and b52aa48. The fixture was last changed in a78fa61, before this
  branch.
- Retained lifecycle checks I read rather than reran (.design/reviews/kan-v2-recovery-opening-author/
  02-tests.txt): attested_lifecycle 11, copy_destination 33, bundle 10, replay 10, store 34, which all pass.
  Surface was 17/2 failed there, and its corrected rerun (07) gives 19/19. Applicability: after 21c6e8e
  the only production source change is src/evidence_recovery_replay.rs. Its only non-test consumer is
  src/evidence_store/bundle.rs (grep), so those lifecycle results still apply.
- Final post-restoration rerun: same 45 integration plus 2 unit functions pass, fmt exit 0 (logs/60, 61).

=====================================================================================================
SCOPE A — PHYSICAL READ-ONLY KNB1 INSPECTOR (src/evidence_store/bundle.rs, bundle.sql)

3. REQUIREMENT COVERAGE (.design/kan-v2-recovery-bundle-opening.md; evidence = code read + commands)
A-R1 Owner-only read-only API: path + independent Context + optional external Checkpoint + budgets; returns
     verified Replay and bounded source identity; no Connection, unverified rows, writer activation,
     standalone fallback or completion flag.
     MET. bundle.rs:270-277 `pub fn inspect(path, context, checkpoint: Option<&Checkpoint>, budget)`.
     Inspection (60-80) exposes only source(), replay(), acquired_bytes(), items(). inspect_snapshot is
     private. Error-only on failure: Inspection is constructed only at 446-451, after replay and check.
A-R2 Exact profile: application_id KNB1, user_version 1, UTF-8.
     MET. 171-175. Author test utf16 asserts Invalid("bundle encoding"). A-M01 schema gate removed: killed
     ("accepted mutation: PRAGMA application_id=...").
A-R3 Exact schema; extra/missing tables/indexes/views/triggers refuse.
     MET. 176-194 compares type/name/tbl_name/sql (bounded substr + full byte length) against an in-memory
     DB built from the same SCHEMA. Probes: ANALYZE stat1, whitespace-only schema edit, CHECK removed via
     writable_schema, schema sql stored as BLOB all give Invalid("bundle schema"). A malformed extra schema
     row gives Sql(DatabaseCorrupt) (A08a-e). rootpage is not compared. I tested that hole with b-tree
     substitution (A02/A03 below): it reduces to ordinary content attacks, which the pure layer refuses.
A-R4 Identity cardinality and every field against caller pins before bulk contents.
     MET. 196-237, called at 341 before any bulk query. A07a second identity row gives "identity
     cardinality". A-M02 killed.
A-R5 Text by byte length, ASCII, NUL exclusion; physical CID spelling equals canonical parse.
     MET IN CODE, UNDER-TESTED (A-F2). 149-151, 155-165. Probes A05a-e: NUL inside a 59-byte cid gives
     "cell truncated"; Unicode / invalid UTF-8 gives "ASCII text"; BLOB key gives "cell storage class".
     Canonical spelling: A01a-c gives "canonical CID spelling" for a 'b'+UPPERCASE body, which the typed
     parser accepts.
A-R6 Every column storage class and protocol length checked independently of DDL CHECKs.
     MET for nonempty cells. 123-154. A06a-c (REAL/TEXT/BLOB integers) give "integer storage class or
     bounds". The author's physical test covers TEXT-for-BLOB and limit+1. PARTIAL overall because of A-F1
     (empty BLOB).
A-R7 Main + existing sidecars: private regular file, symlink refusal, mutual inode aliasing before open;
     source-byte budget is a pre-open observation.
     MET as declared. 299-322. A-M09 alias check removed: killed. A-M10 source budget removed: killed.
     A09d: the budget counts -wal/-shm. A11a/b: a directory -shm or FIFO -wal gives "expected regular
     database file". Declared scope, not defects: a symlinked PARENT directory is accepted (A11c), and a
     second hard link of the main file elsewhere is accepted (A11d). Only the final component and mutual
     aliasing are fenced, as the design says.
A-R8 Explicit SQLite coordination capability; read-only open may create WAL/SHM; no filesystem-purity claim.
     MET. persistence.rs:202-210 (READ_ONLY flags), SurfaceWrite::EvidenceBundleSource (+2 surfaces), one
     call site bundle.rs:323-327, TSV rows, RULE_EVIDENCE, PERSISTENCE_MUTATION_SITES, updated facade digest.
     A-M07 wrong capability fails the INDEPENDENT inventory semantically (surface_conformance.rs:1393:
     "labels evidence-bundle-source:database-wal with capability EvidenceRecoverySource, whose allowed
     artifacts are [evidence-recovery-source:...]"). A09c: with -shm removed, the reader recreates -shm
     (mode 600), and main and -wal bytes are unchanged.
A-R9 Hot rollback journal refuses; preserve source media.
     MET. A10a: Sql(ReadOnly, extended 776 = SQLITE_READONLY_ROLLBACK). The author test also checks that
     main and journal bytes are unchanged. A-M11 (READ_WRITE open) is killed: the test asserts refusal,
     and the mutant ACCEPTS after silently rolling the journal back into the source. A10b: an empty,
     non-hot journal is accepted and retained.
A-R10 query-only, SQL length limits, bounded cache, busy timeout, deadline/cancellation before first schema/
     data read; one pinned transaction; no immutable=1.
     MET IN CODE. 328-339: LIMIT_LENGTH 5 MiB, busy_timeout ≤250 ms, progress handler, then query_only /
     trusted_schema=OFF / cache_size / mmap 0 / BEGIN. No immutable. SQLITE_LIMIT_SQL_LENGTH is not set,
     but schema text is already bounded by LIMIT_LENGTH at column fetch (info). A-M05 (no BEGIN): killed
     semantically ("Replay(Invalid(\"observation authentication\"))", the later WAL row mixed in). A09a
     reads committed-but-uncheckpointed WAL frames consistently (latest=6, versus 7 from the main file
     alone), with main and wal unchanged. A-M13 (no query_only) SURVIVES: redundant with READ_ONLY flags.
A-R11 Busy wait and SQLite VM cancellation behavior must be tested.
     PARTIAL (A-F3). Busy is tested (author, <3 s). VM-level deadline/cancellation is NOT tested: A-M08
     (progress handler removed) passes the entire author bundle suite and both units. My probe A12 (a
     400,007-row schema; plain load 17.5-18.7 s) shows the real code stops in 162 ms (deadline 150 ms) and
     125 ms (cancel at 100 ms). Under A-M08 both take ~17.5 s.
A-R12 Budget acquisition before materializing; rows and encoded field bytes separate from replay scan bytes;
     charge before copy; overflow rejected; report which limit failed; no universal cap.
     MET. 81-115, 152 (charge before to_vec), checked_add. Author test edges: items and bytes exact±1,
     source, replay separate, cancel, duration 0. A13: 3601 s gives Invalid("duration") and 3600 s accepts.
     Info: the final `work.check()?` (455) relabels an independent error, or discards a completed result,
     as duration/cancel if the deadline passes between completion and return. Conservative, a race only.
A-R13 Bounded substring probes; avoid WITHOUT ROWID key seeks; canonical PK order scan, no arbitrary sort;
     non-BLOB / malformed key / oversized cell is a forensic-format refusal, not a missing row.
     MET (labels: A-F4). NOT INDEXED ORDER BY pk scans. A04a-f: >5 MiB cells in BLOB value, TEXT key
     (WITHOUT ROWID), observation, identity text, manifest and membership key all give
     Sql(TooBig "string or blob too big"), never a missing row. Peak RSS with a 56 MiB corrupt original is
     13.1 MB, versus 14.7 MB for a normal fixture (probes/rss-oversized.log), so it is not materialized.
     A04g (4 MiB+1) gives Invalid("integer storage class or bounds"). B-tree tampering behind canonical
     schema text: duplicate keys (A02a-c) and descending storage order (A03a-b) reach the pure layer and
     refuse ("candidate order or duplicate" / "CID order or duplicate"); the ascending-twin control
     (A03c) accepts.
A-R14 Preserve empty or hash-invalid original BLOB bytes within the 4-MiB cell limit; candidates nonempty
     and hash-valid.
     UNMET for empty originals: A-F1. Hash-invalid nonempty originals: MET (corpus case
     original-object-basis-survives-restoration; my E3 control accepts).
A-R15 Validation: Python fixtures from signed corpus; profile 2, complete and partial profile 3,
     CORRUPT/EMPTY originals, restored candidates, multiple attempts, external checkpoint extensions; the
     refusal list; standalone escape refusal.
     PARTIAL. 13 accepted / 32 refused physical reproductions with main-byte preservation hold
     (python_sqlite_histories...). But NO corpus case contains an empty original (I enumerated all 45
     cases), and the one constructed by me is refused (A-F1). The refusal list is covered except as noted
     in A-F2/A-F4. Standalone: 6 file readers refuse (author test). Root-based Ledger/Archive::open and
     inventory/copy-upgrade entries share RecoveryReader profile checks but are not exercised directly
     (low, A-F6).
A-R16 Python fixtures are not a second semantic-schema oracle; runtime SQL equals the previous fixture.
     MET, and labelled honestly (recovery_bundle_files.py docstring; opening.md).
A-R17 No creator/restorer/publisher/signing/job/RPC/UI; no parent AC closes.
     MET. bundle.rs has no write path. Every AC-1..AC-6 checkbox in kan-v2-recovery-bundles.md is still
     "[ ]".

4. SCOPE A FINDINGS
A-F1 [BLOCKING — correctness; fail-closed false refusal of a design-mandated state]
  Code: bundle.rs:144-147
      let bytes = match (text, row.get_ref(col + 2)?) {
          (true, ValueRef::Text(b)) | (false, ValueRef::Blob(b)) => b,
          _ => return Err(Error::Invalid("projected cell storage class")),
  The projection is substr(bytes,1,4194304) (167-169, 253). SQLite substr() returns NULL for a zero-length
  BLOB. Bundled sqlite3.c (3.53.2) substrFunc: `z = sqlite3_value_blob(argv[0]); if( z==0 ) return;`, and
  sqlite3_value_blob returns `p->n ? p->z : 0`. Confirmed independently: probes/empty-blob-substr-python.txt
  gives typeof(substr(x'',1,N)) = 'null'.
  Requirement violated: opening.md "Preserve empty or hash-invalid original BLOB bytes within the 4-MiB
  cell limit". The DDL allows `length(bytes) BETWEEN 0 AND 4194304`. Validation requires "corrupt/empty
  originals". The author REPORT claims "Original corrupt/empty BLOBs remain exact retained evidence."
  Demonstration (independent signed histories, probes/gen_physical_probes.py, run1 log):
    E1 empty original, initial loss: pure replay ACCEPT latest=2 | Python oracle accept | PHYSICAL REFUSE
       Invalid("projected cell storage class")
    E2 empty original + valid restoration: pure ACCEPT latest=3 restored=1 | oracle accept | PHYSICAL REFUSE
    E3 identical shape, 1-byte corrupt original: pure ACCEPT | PHYSICAL ACCEPT (control)
  Impact: retained empty-original evidence (a truncated-to-zero object, exactly the corruption bundles
  exist to retain) makes the whole bundle uninspectable. Nothing is accepted wrongly and nothing is
  rewritten. Source unchanged (E1-E3 source-unchanged=true).
  Required: accept a NULL projection only when typeof='blob' and length=0 (the parent edit observed in
  §0 has this shape but is unreviewed). Add signed empty-original physical vectors (profile 2, and a
  partial profile 3 if reachable) for both initial-loss and restored histories. Keep candidates
  nonempty. Re-run the controls, and give this a fresh review.
A-F2 [MEDIUM-LOW — test gap; author survivor classification is wrong in general]
  The author recorded the canonical-key control as a redundant-defense survivor because "the typed CID
  parser already rejects the tested uppercase representation". That holds only for the tested spelling
  upper(cid), whose 'B' prefix the DASL parser rejects. The multibase base32lower decoder translates
  uppercase body characters (multibase-0.9.3 encoding.rs:24-28 translate_from "A..Z"), so 'b'+UPPERCASE
  parses to the same CID. Under A-M03 the author test passes (SURVIVES, reproduced), while my probes show
  hostile acceptance of non-canonical physical keys in all three key tables:
    A01a restored_objects ACCEPT latest=7, A01b member_objects ACCEPT latest=6, A01c member_membership
    ACCEPT latest=7 (mutations/A-M03-canonical-key.txt). Unmutated: all three give "canonical CID spelling".
  The guard is load-bearing, not redundant. Required: add a parser-accepted non-canonical spelling to the
  physical refusal test, and reclassify the control as demonstrated.
A-F3 [LOW-MEDIUM — required test absent]
  The design requires that SQLite VM cancellation be tested. A-M08 (progress handler removed) survives the
  entire author suite. My A12 probe kills it by timing (deadline 150 ms: 162 ms real versus 17,539 ms
  mutant; cancel 100 ms: 125 ms versus 17,471 ms). Required: promote a bounded long-VM-step test (e.g. a
  large schema load) that asserts elapsed time well below the unbounded load time.
A-F4 [LOW — error taxonomy]
  Oversized (>5 MiB) cells, hot journals and malformed schema surface as raw Error::Sql (TooBig /
  READONLY_ROLLBACK 776 / DatabaseCorrupt), not a typed forensic-format refusal. Refusal is correct and is
  never a missing-row conversion. But the author suite asserts only is_err() and tests only limit+1, never
  >5 MiB. Follow-up: map these to a typed refusal (or document Sql as that channel) and assert the kind.
